title: Grateful Dead Live at Crystal Ballroom on 1968-02-02

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a primal February‑68 show with blistering Jerry solos, epic Viola Lee Blues and soaring Clementine, recorded well enough to let the fireworks shine.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of early ’68’s finest – a wild, psychedelic burst anchored by an explosive Viola Lee Blues, a jazzy, transcendent Clementine, and a tight Other One suite.  Although the tape is described as a bit muddy or “rough,” it is still a soundboard source that many find clear enough to enjoy the high‑energy playing throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, almost all 5‑star, praising both the music and the recording; only minor complaints about muddiness keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as a bit muddy or rough compared to later shows, but still clear enough for listeners; many note the tape’s power and presence despite occasional lack of polish.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise, high‑octane early‑68 set that jumps from garage‑blues to soaring psychedelia and jazzy improvisation, showcasing the band’s rapid evolution toward the Anthem era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for blistering tone, soaring solos and “wailing” on his Les Paul or SG; described as a highlight of the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for solid bass work, especially counting time during Clementine and keeping the groove tight.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s harmonica and vocal power are highlighted as essential blues energy throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Mentions of Brent (and occasional Keith) solos; Brent’s playing described as “god‑like” in one review.
